messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- As a follow-up to INC-2026-009, the scheduler leader lease will be shortened to ten seconds. [decision; valid 2026-05-08 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-009]
- Notifier consumers will commit offsets every five seconds. [decision; valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- On 2026-05-04, Team Boreal decided that the event bus will retain messages for seven days, because replaying a full week has covered every incident recovery so far. [decision; valid 2026-05-04 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2026-05-04]
- On 2025-07-03, Team Atlas flagged that the notifier's memory use grew steadily for a week following the cache change, noting the notifier is not their service. [valid 2025-07-03 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-07-03-2]
- On 2025-09-08, Team Boreal noticed that the notifier's request volume halved after the client rollout and pinged the owners. [valid 2025-09-08 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-09-08-2]
- The notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff. [decision; valid 2025-02-20 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-20]
- The notifier's flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages. [valid 2025-02-20 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-20]
- As of 2025-06-19, the notifier lives with Team Dune. [valid 2025-06-19 to now; recorded by handover/2025-06-19-notifier]
    earlier: As of 2025-04-04, the notifier lives with Team Cinder. [valid 2025-04-04 to 2025-06-19; recorded by handover/2025-04-04-notifier]
    earlier: The notifier lives with Team Boreal. [valid 2025-01-09 to 2025-04-04; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-01-09-2]
- On 2026-01-22, the team decided the webhooks service will require an idempotency key on every delivery, because the duplicate deliveries in INC-2026-003 came from retries without one. [decision; valid 2026-01-22 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- The notifier depends on the event bus for delivery events. [valid 2025-01-17 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-01-17]
- On 2025-06-12, Team Dune noticed the notifier's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift and pinged the owners. [valid 2025-06-12 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-06-12]
- INC-2025-004 was an incident affecting the notifier on 2025-02-06. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- The catalog service's joined writes were locking product updates for seconds at a time. [valid 2025-04-04 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-04-04]
- On 2025-12-17, Team Dune decided that the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write. [decision; valid 2025-12-17 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-12-17]
- The scheduler's previous single fixed node turned every restart into a missed run. [valid 2025-06-13 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-06-13]
- Team Dune's planning meeting is every Wednesday. [valid 2025-11-06 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-11-06-2]
- The scheduler pulls per-job kill switches from the feature-flags service on every run. [valid 2025-03-28 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-03-28]
- On 2025-07-28, Team Cinder decided that clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds. [decision; valid 2025-07-28 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-07-28]
- On 2026-03-19, the Ember team noticed that the scheduler's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump and pinged the owners. [valid 2026-03-19 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2026-03-19-2]
- On 2026-05-25, Team Atlas reported that the webhooks service's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change. [valid 2026-05-25 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-05-25-2]

Question: Why do notifier consumers commit offsets every five seconds?
